intended_object: The realization functor Pro(FinSet) → Profinite, sending a pro-finite set (a cofiltered formal limit of finite sets, encoded as (Ind FinSetᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ) to the profinite space given by its limit. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the full-faithfulness results later in the file.
explanation: On objects, the definition takes the chosen Ind-presentation of Q.unop. Its index category is filtered, so its opposite is cofiltered; flipping the diagram gives a cofiltered diagram of finite sets, and the functor returns its limit in Profinite (Profinite.limitCone). This is the standard realization of a pro-object. On morphisms, a morphism is transported along the presentation isomorphisms (indDualPresentationIso). It is then sent to a continuous map between the limits by finiteDiagramIndDualContinuousEquiv, which goes from Ind-morphisms (stagewise classes) to compatible maps on finite stages and then to continuous maps between the limits. The functor laws are proved from the identity and composition lemmas for that comparison, and the file later proves the functor is fully faithful, as expected of Pro(FinSet) → Profinite. The construction depends on the chosen presentations only up to canonical isomorphism, which the file makes explicit with comparison isomorphisms to any limiting cone. Using FintypeCat.Skeleton is a technical requirement, because Mathlib's Ind needs a small category, and the skeleton is equivalent to FintypeCat. The construction needs its specific setting, since the target Profinite only makes sense for limits of finite discrete sets, so it is not too narrow. Searching Mathlib for Ind FintypeCat, Pro FintypeCat and a Pro definition found nothing, so Mathlib has no pro-category of finite sets and no such realization functor.
